peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the germ that causes Newcastle disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Newcastle disease is caused by virulent strains of avian paramyxovirus type 1 (aka Newcastle disease virus). The disease has no pathognomonic clinical signs or lesions; laboratory confirmation is needed for diagnosis.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Newcastle Disease in Poultry - MSD Veterinary Manual

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Is Newcastle disease a viral disease?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Newcastle disease (ND) is a highly contagious and often severe disease found worldwide that affects birds including domestic poultry. It is caused by a virus in the family of paramyxoviruses.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Newcastle disease - WOAH - World Organisation for Animal Health

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the DNA of the Newcastle virus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet:
GENOME ANNOUNCEMENT

 Newcastle disease virus (NDV) is a member of the genus Avulavirus in the family Paramyxoviridae. The genome of NDV is a single-stranded, negative-sense, nonsegmented RNA with six genes encoding seven major viral proteins (1).

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Is Newcastle disease airborne?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Newcastle disease virus has been shown to survive when airborne in small particles, both in the laboratory and in the open air.
